subject: Ingress strategy playbook — Peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Hawkins <sam.hawkins@astramed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Oct 2025 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Ingress strategy playbook — Peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN

Hi Sam —

Thanks for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I pulled together a short playbook that outlines the operational tradeoffs between three typical connectivity patterns for Redwood Private: VPC peering (cross-account peering), PrivateLink (interface endpoints / managed endpoint), and site-to-site (S2S) VPN. The goal here is to map each option to AstraMed's constraints so you can pick an initial onboarding path with a clear fallback.

Key AstraMed constraints I heard on the call:
- Outbound egress to third-party cloud endpoints must pass through your egress proxy and be audited (no direct internet egress allowed from the subnet that holds sensitive PHI inference traffic).
- You need consistent tail latency <= 40ms for interactive clinical lookups across your east-us region.
- Initial POC must be completed inside 2–3 weeks and prefer minimal infra changes.

High-level recommendations (short):
- PrivateLink as primary: meets the egress/control needs without exposing tenant VPC IP ranges; supports endpoint-level IAM and NACLs, aligns with your audit requirements when used with proxying and VPC flow logs. Slightly higher per-GB cost but simpler security posture.
- VPC peering for high-throughput low-cost path: great if you can accept cross-account routing and configure egress proxying in the peered VPC; lacks interface endpoint control and is harder if you need fine-grained service-level routing.
- S2S VPN for quick POC: fastest to stand up using your edge firewall; good for initial functional validation but not recommended for long-term production because of bandwidth/latency variability and lack of cloud-native auth controls.

I've attached a short playbook and a MOP draft for PrivateLink. Ben and Kim — can you add any operational constraints I missed (autoscaling, MTU, route table hygiene, expected throughput/per-GB estimates) and confirm we can hit a 2–3 week POC timeline with PrivateLink + the MOP?

Sam — once we align we'll put up a short runbook for your NetOps and schedule a 1-hour working session with your firewall team.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Ingress strategy playbook — Peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN

Neha, thanks for the note and the quick summary — super helpful. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Egress audit: our compliance team requires that any upstream cloud endpoint used for inference traffic is reachable only through our outbound proxy (the proxy performs URL allow-listing and TLS inspection). We cannot have an IP route that bypasses that path for PHI-bound traffic.
- Firewall: our perimeter boxes support on-prem IPSec for S2S; we can also accept a PrivateLink approach if the interface endpoint IPs are routed to the proxy. Not sure yet on how the proxy interacts with ENIs.
- Throughput: POC will be light (spokes will hit <200 Mbps), but production could be multi-Gbps. We need a solution that scales.

Given the above I agree PrivateLink looks attractive, but we need a clear pattern for forcing egress via our proxy (we can't have endpoint-to-internet behavior). Also curious about certificate/broker integration for mTLS to Redwood.

Open to the 1-hr working session; can do Tue or Wed next week.

—Sam
Network Architect, AstraMed

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Sam Hawkins <sam.hawkins@astramed.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Oct 2025 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ingress strategy playbook — Peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN

Thanks Sam — good notes. A few operational points I want to call out so expectations are clear:

PrivateLink (interface endpoint) — pros/cons and mitigations:
- Pros: endpoint-level access control (SGs + IAM), no need to expose tenant IP ranges to Redwood, easier to certify from an audit perspective.
- Egress proxying: two patterns we use:
  1) Route the endpoint ENIs to a dedicated subnet that forces outbound to your egress proxy via a default route + NACL. That subnet holds the interface endpoint ENIs and a small NAT device if needed. This preserves inspection while keeping traffic off the public internet.
  2) Use a proxy appliance in your VPC (sidecar or gateway) that accepts traffic from the endpoint ENIs and performs TLS termination/re-encryption. This requires certificate trust between Redwood and AstraMed.
- Cost: PrivateLink has per-hour and per-GB charges; for heavy sustained throughput VPC peering is cheaper.

VPC Peering — constraints:
- Peering requires explicitly adding routes in your route table to send traffic to Redwood's peered VPC. If you cannot guarantee your egress proxy will inspect that peered path, it becomes non-compliant. Also peering is transitive: cross-account peering doesn't provide service-level gating.

S2S VPN — quick POC option:
- Good for functional validation; we can stand up a managed VPN terminator in Redwood's edge and peer it into your firewall quickly.
- Not ideal in production for your multi-Gbps needs unless you go with dedicated DX/Direct Connect equivalent.

Operational ask from Redwood: if we proceed with PrivateLink, we'll need:
- A contact from your NetOps for ENI placement and routing decisions.
- Agreement on TLS flow: either mTLS between client and Redwood or mutual TLS at proxy boundary.
- Expected throughput profile for sizing and cost estimates.

Neha — if you can confirm the MOP items I'll sign off and we can propose Wed 14th 11:00 AM PT for the working session.

Ben
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Sam — thanks for the quick reply and the constraints.

Summary / next steps:
- Primary recommendation: PrivateLink + endpoint-enforced egress to your proxy (pattern #1 from Ben). This satisfies the audit requirement while giving you service-level control.
- Fallback: VPC peering only if your compliance team signs off on peered path inspection. We'll document the route controls and an explicit non-transitive peering agreement.
- POC plan: stand up PrivateLink in a staging VPC, route endpoint ENIs to proxy subnet, run small-scale traffic (up to 200 Mbps) for 2 weeks, confirm latency and observability.

Action items:
- Sam / NetOps: share an IAM contact and a short firewall config checklist (we'll bring a template).
- Ben / Infra: finalize the MOP (attached) and add MTU/keepalive guidance.
- Kim / Solutions: size expected per-GB costs and estimated Latency SLO impact.

Proposed working session: Wed, 15 Oct 2025 11:00 AM PT — I'll send a calendar invite and include a pre-read (attached).

Thanks all — looking forward to moving this to POC.
